Definition: from G4862 and G3854; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid:--come together, stand with.
BiblicalUsage: After the crucifixion all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts and returned. They had come to watch a spectacle and went home beating their breasts, because what they saw would not let them stay as they were.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that standing at the cross changes the watcher, and I hold that no one who truly sees what happened there goes home unchanged.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
